newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Austrian U.N. observer released by Tajik gunmen.
newsitem.headline: Austrian U.N. observer released by Tajik gunmen.

text.p: The United Nations in Tajikistan said on Tuesday one of four military observers held hostage by armed rebels had been released and had returned to Dushanbe, the capital of the former Soviet republic.

"One hostage, a U.N. military observer, Major G. Hoenig, has been released," a spokesman for the U.N. in Dushanbe told Reuters. Hoenig, an Austrian national, was said by the U.N. to be seriously ill throughout the country's eight-day hostage crisis.

Earlier on Tuesday, the Tajik government said it would bow to the demands of the rebel group holding several U.N. officials hostage by allowing the return of 40 fellow fighters from neighbouring Afghanistan.

The hostage crisis began early last week when the rebels, led by Bakhrom Sadirov, seized four United Nations military observers. They later captured a carload of Russian reporters and four workers with the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR.
The crisis worsened on Saturday when the rebels seized Tajik Security Minister Saidamir Zukharov who had flown in to negotiate with the hostage-takers.

The kidnappings come just as the government and Islamist opposition rebels are trying to end a bitter four-year civil war that has left tens of thousands dead and many more homeless. But the Tajik president and the leader of the opposition said on Tuesday they would not let the hostage crisis end efforts to negotiate a settlement.
